ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Computer vision methods for recognizing human activity. One of the great problems in computer vision is to say what people are doing from a picture or a video of them doing it. There are numerous applications, ranging from building models of how people behave to advance architectural design, to surveillance. This problem is very hard indeed, for several reasons. There is not a clean vocabulary for what people are doing, particularly for everyday activity. Often, the interesting stuff is very rare indeed, and people just walk. People can do a lot of different things. Finally, what they're doing looks different when seen from different angles. The course will involve a series of lectures, discussions and paper readings. Class meets in 3405 SC.
